title: SC-300 Domain 4 questions (4.1, 4.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Microsoft.

questions.stem: The marketing lead at Fabrikam must be able to create new catalogs for her department's resources and manage them herself. She must not hold any Microsoft Entra administrator role. What should you do?
choices: Assign her the Identity Governance Administrator role
Make her a catalog owner of the General catalog
Add her to the Catalog creator role in entitlement management
Assign her the Groups Administrator role so she can manage all groups
questions.answer: Add her to the Catalog creator role in entitlement management
questions.explanation: Catalog creator is an entitlement management role, not a directory role, and lets a user create catalogs and become owner of the ones they create. Being an owner of the General catalog only lets her manage that one catalog; it does not let her create new ones.

questions.stem: A help desk analyst at Tailspin Toys must add and remove users from the access packages in the Sales catalog. The analyst must not change any policy or resource in those access packages. Which role should you assign, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Access package assignment manager
Access package manager
Catalog owner
Catalog reader
questions.answer: Access package assignment manager
questions.explanation: An access package assignment manager can manage assignments and requests for the catalog's access packages but cannot edit their policies or resources. An access package manager can also create and edit access packages and policies, which is more than the analyst needs.

questions.stem: A project manager at Contoso must create access packages and edit their request policies in the Projects catalog, using only resources that are already in that catalog. Which role should you assign, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Catalog owner
Access package assignment manager
Catalog creator
Access package manager
questions.answer: Access package manager
questions.explanation: An access package manager can create and manage access packages and their policies from the resources already in a catalog. A catalog owner can also add resources and manage catalog roles, which goes beyond what is required.

questions.stem: In Microsoft Entra entitlement management, what is a catalog?
choices: A list of the enterprise applications that are published through Application Proxy
A container of resources and access packages with its own delegated owners
A report of each user's current group memberships and roles
A Conditional Access template that grants access to app bundles
questions.answer: A container of resources and access packages with its own delegated owners
questions.explanation: A catalog groups resources (groups, applications, SharePoint Online sites) and the access packages built from them, and can be delegated to catalog owners and other catalog roles. It is not a report or a Conditional Access construct.

questions.stem: A catalog owner at Northwind Traders tries to add the HR-Readers security group to the HR catalog, but the group cannot be selected. The catalog owner holds no Microsoft Entra administrator role. What should you do so the catalog owner can add the group?
choices: Assign the catalog owner the Catalog reader role on the HR catalog
Make the catalog owner an owner of the security group
Convert the security group to a Microsoft 365 group
Enable the catalog for external users
questions.answer: Make the catalog owner an owner of the security group
questions.explanation: To add a resource to a catalog, a user without a suitable administrator role must be a catalog owner and also own the resource. The Catalog reader role only grants view access and would not help.

questions.stem: Contoso wants every member user in the tenant, but no guest users, to be able to request the Finance Tools access package. Which option should the policy use for who can request access?
choices: For users in your directory: All users (including guests)
For users not in your directory: All configured connected organizations
None (administrator direct assignments only)
For users in your directory: All members (excluding guests)
questions.answer: For users in your directory: All members (excluding guests)
questions.explanation: The All members (excluding guests) option lets every member user request while excluding guests. All users (including guests) would also let existing guest users request the package.

questions.stem: Adatum uses an access package to give contractors access to a build system. Only administrators may assign the package, and users must not be able to submit requests for it in any way. Which policy option should you choose?
choices: None (administrator direct assignments only)
Mark the access package as hidden in My Access
For users in your directory: Specific users and groups
Require two stages of approval for every request
questions.answer: None (administrator direct assignments only)
questions.explanation: A policy that allows only administrator direct assignments means no user can request the package. Marking a package as hidden only removes it from the My Access search; users with the direct link could still request it.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes an access package in entitlement management?
choices: A set of Conditional Access policies that apply to one group
A single group membership that can never be set to expire
A bundle of resource roles with policies that define who can get them
A list of Microsoft Entra roles that eligible users activate through PIM
questions.answer: A bundle of resource roles with policies that define who can get them
questions.explanation: An access package bundles resource roles (group membership, application roles, SharePoint Online site roles) with one or more policies that control who can request, approval, and lifecycle. It is not a Conditional Access or PIM object.

questions.stem: An access package manager at Litware is building a new access package, but the Project Docs SharePoint Online site does not appear in the list of available resources. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: SharePoint Online sites cannot be included in access packages
The site must first be connected to a Microsoft 365 group
Access package managers can include only applications in packages
The site has not been added to the catalog that holds the package
questions.answer: The site has not been added to the catalog that holds the package
questions.explanation: Access package managers can only use resources that are already in the catalog; a catalog owner must add the site first. SharePoint Online sites are a supported resource type, so that distractor is false.

questions.stem: Approvers of the Research Data access package at Fabrikam need each requester to state a project code and an end date in the request. What should you configure in the access package policy?
choices: A terms of use document that the requester must open and accept
A second approval stage assigned to the project leads
Requestor information questions that the requester must answer
A custom security attribute on each requester account
questions.answer: Requestor information questions that the requester must answer
questions.explanation: Requestor information lets you add questions to the request form, and the answers are shown to approvers. A terms of use document records acceptance of a document; it does not collect project-specific answers.

questions.stem: At Wingtip Toys, requests for the Payroll Viewer access package must be approved first by the requester's manager and then by a member of the Security Reviewers group. What should you configure?
choices: One approval stage that lists both the manager and Security Reviewers
Two approval stages: the manager first, then Security Reviewers
Security Reviewers as an incompatible group on the package
A monthly access review of the package with both as reviewers
questions.answer: Two approval stages: the manager first, then Security Reviewers
questions.explanation: Sequential approval needs separate stages; the request moves to the second stage only after the first stage approves. In a single stage with several approvers, a decision by any one of them is enough, so the manager alone could approve.

questions.stem: An access package policy uses the requester's manager as the approver. Some requests at Contoso cannot be routed because the requester has no manager set in Microsoft Entra ID. What should you configure?
choices: Fallback approvers for the stage that uses the manager
Alternate approvers who receive requests after a timeout
Requestor justification for every request in the policy
An expiration date on the access package assignments
questions.answer: Fallback approvers for the stage that uses the manager
questions.explanation: Fallback approvers are used when the manager or sponsor approver cannot be found. Alternate approvers handle requests that the first approvers do not act on in time, not missing managers.

questions.stem: Approvers for the Vendor Portal access package at Tailspin Toys are often away. If they do not act on a request within three days, the request must go to the operations team. What should you configure?
choices: Alternate approvers, forwarding requests after three days without a decision
Fallback approvers for the approval stage
A request timeout of three days so the request expires
A second approval stage that is assigned to the operations team members
questions.answer: Alternate approvers, forwarding requests after three days without a decision
questions.explanation: Alternate approvers receive the request when the original approvers have not decided after the configured number of days. A second stage would require both groups to approve, and fallback approvers are only used when the approver cannot be determined.

questions.stem: A single approval stage in an access package policy lists three approvers. How many of them must approve a request for it to move forward?
choices: All three of the listed approvers
Any one of the listed approvers
A majority of the listed approvers
Only the first approver in the list
questions.answer: Any one of the listed approvers
questions.explanation: Within a stage, the first decision by any listed approver applies to the request. Requiring several independent approvals is done with multiple approval stages instead.

questions.stem: Contractors at Northwind Traders request the Summer Project access package at different times, but all of their access must end on September 30. How should you configure the policy's expiration?
choices: Assignments expire a set number of days after approval
Assignments never expire and are reviewed every quarter
Assignments expire on a specific date of September 30
Assignments never expire, and users may request extensions
questions.answer: Assignments expire on a specific date of September 30
questions.explanation: Choosing a specific date ends every assignment from that policy on the same day, whenever the request was approved. A number of days would end access at different times for each contractor.

questions.stem: Interns at Adatum receive the Intern Tools access package for 90 days. Interns who still need access must be able to ask for more time before their assignment ends, without submitting a brand new request. What should you configure?
choices: Set the policy's assignments to never expire
Add a second approval stage to the policy
Add Intern Tools as its own incompatible access package
Allow users to extend access in the policy's expiration settings
questions.answer: Allow users to extend access in the policy's expiration settings
questions.explanation: Allowing extension lets users with an expiring assignment request more time from My Access, and the request goes through the policy's approval settings. Removing expiration would leave access open-ended.

questions.stem: To enforce separation of duties at Contoso, users who already have the Payments Approver access package must not be able to request the Payments Creator access package. What should you configure?
choices: Require two approval stages on Payments Creator
Move the two access packages into separate catalogs
Add Payments Approver as an incompatible package on Payments Creator
Schedule a recurring access review of the Payments Approver assignments
questions.answer: Add Payments Approver as an incompatible package on Payments Creator
questions.explanation: Incompatible access packages on Payments Creator block requests from users who already hold Payments Approver. Approval stages or separate catalogs do not stop an approver from granting both packages to the same person.

questions.stem: Members of the Internal Auditors security group at Fabrikam, which is managed outside entitlement management, must not be able to request the Finance Admin access package. What should you configure?
choices: Add Internal Auditors as an incompatible group on Finance Admin
Exclude Internal Auditors from a Conditional Access policy
Change the policy to All members (excluding guests)
Remove the Internal Auditors group from the catalog
questions.answer: Add Internal Auditors as an incompatible group on Finance Admin
questions.explanation: Incompatible groups block requests from users who are members of the specified group, even when that membership is managed elsewhere. A Conditional Access exclusion controls sign-in, not who can request an access package.

questions.stem: Before turning on separation of duties checks between two access packages, a Litware administrator wants to know which users already hold assignments to both. What should you use?
choices: The Microsoft Entra sign-in logs filtered by application
The Identity Secure Score improvement actions
The catalog's list of resources and resource roles
A list of users who already have incompatible access
questions.answer: A list of users who already have incompatible access
questions.explanation: Entitlement management can list users who already have access that conflicts with a package's incompatible settings, so you can clean it up first. New checks only block future requests; they do not remove existing conflicting assignments.

questions.stem: Assignments to the Partner Collaboration access package at Wingtip Toys never expire. Each quarter, the sponsor of each assigned user must confirm that the access is still needed, and denied users must lose the package. What should you configure with the LEAST administrative effort?
choices: A Teams + Groups review of each group in the package
Access reviews in the access package's assignment policy
An expiration date that is changed by hand every quarter
Lifecycle workflows that run when a user's manager changes
questions.answer: Access reviews in the access package's assignment policy
questions.explanation: A policy can include recurring access reviews of its assignments, and denied users lose the whole access package. Reviewing the underlying groups separately would remove group membership but leave the access package assignment in place.

questions.stem: Where do users at Contoso go to request access packages and to approve the requests that are routed to them?
choices: The My Apps portal
The My Access portal
The My Account portal
The Microsoft Entra admin center
questions.answer: The My Access portal
questions.explanation: Requesters browse, request and extend access packages in My Access, and approvers act on requests there too. My Apps launches applications, and My Account manages a user's own profile and security info.

questions.stem: A request for the Engineering access package at Adatum shows a status of Delivery failed because one SharePoint Online site was briefly unavailable. The site is now available. What should you do with the LEAST administrative effort?
choices: Ask the user to cancel and submit a new request
Delete the access package and create it again
Add the user to each resource by hand
Reprocess the request
questions.answer: Reprocess the request
questions.explanation: Reprocessing retries delivery of a failed or partially delivered request without another approval cycle. Asking for a new request repeats the approval process for no reason.

questions.stem: A user at Tailspin Toys submitted a request for the wrong access package, and the request is still pending approval. As an administrator, what should you do?
choices: Cancel the pending request
Remove the user's access package assignment
Delete the access package's request policy
Start an access review of the access package
questions.answer: Cancel the pending request
questions.explanation: A pending request can be canceled by an administrator or the requester, so no approver acts on it. There is no assignment yet, so removing an assignment does nothing.

questions.stem: A new hire at Fabrikam needs the Onboarding access package today, and an administrator wants to grant it immediately while keeping the package's expiration settings. What should the administrator do?
choices: Add the user to each of the package's groups by hand
Remove the approval stage from the package's policy
Directly assign the user to the access package
Add the user as a reviewer of the access package
questions.answer: Directly assign the user to the access package
questions.explanation: A direct assignment by an administrator grants the package right away and applies the selected policy's lifecycle settings, such as expiration. Adding the user to each group by hand bypasses entitlement management, so nothing would remove that access later.

questions.stem: An auditor asks Northwind Traders for a list of users who currently hold the Treasury access package and the date each assignment ends. What should you use?
choices: The Conditional Access What If tool for each user
The provisioning logs for the Treasury application
The catalog's resource roles and their owners
The access package's assignments list, downloaded as a file
questions.answer: The access package's assignments list, downloaded as a file
questions.explanation: The assignments view of an access package shows who holds it, with start and end dates, and can be downloaded. The What If tool evaluates Conditional Access policies and says nothing about assignments.

questions.stem: When a user at Litware is granted the Field Sales access package, an Azure Logic Apps workflow must create the user's account in an external commission system. What should you configure?
choices: A Conditional Access policy that targets the Logic App
An app registration with a separate client secret created for each user
A custom extension on the access package that calls the Logic App
A connected organization for the commission system
questions.answer: A custom extension on the access package that calls the Logic App
questions.explanation: Custom extensions let entitlement management call an Azure Logic App at points such as when an assignment is granted. A connected organization represents an external directory of users, not a downstream system to provision.

questions.stem: Guest users at Contoso must accept a non-disclosure agreement before they can open the Projects SharePoint Online site. What should you implement?
choices: Company branding sign-in text that describes the agreement
Terms of use, required by a Conditional Access policy that targets guests
Requestor justification in the access package policy
Inbound cross-tenant access settings that trust MFA from the partner tenants
questions.answer: Terms of use, required by a Conditional Access policy that targets guests
questions.explanation: A terms of use document enforced through the Conditional Access grant control blocks access until the user accepts it, and records the acceptance. Company branding text is only displayed; it does not capture consent.

questions.stem: In which file format must you upload a terms of use document to Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: PDF
Microsoft Word (DOCX)
HTML
Plain text (TXT)
questions.answer: PDF
questions.explanation: Terms of use documents are uploaded as PDF files, with an optional separate PDF for each language. Word, HTML and plain text files are not accepted.

questions.stem: Adatum's legal team requires that each user accepts the terms of use again 90 days after that user's last acceptance. Which setting should you configure?
choices: Duration before re-acceptance required (days), set to 90
Expire consents, set to a quarterly frequency
Require users to consent on every device
Require users to expand the terms of use
questions.answer: Duration before re-acceptance required (days), set to 90
questions.explanation: Duration before re-acceptance counts from each user's own acceptance date. Expire consents resets acceptance for everyone on a fixed schedule from a start date, so users who accepted recently would be asked again early.

questions.stem: The legal team at Wingtip Toys requires that users open and view the terms of use document before they can accept it. Which setting should you enable?
choices: Require users to consent on every device
Require users to expand the terms of use
Expire consents on a yearly schedule
Add a language version of the document
questions.answer: Require users to expand the terms of use
questions.explanation: Requiring users to expand the terms of use makes them open the document before the Accept button works. Consent on every device controls where acceptance is needed, not whether the document is viewed.

questions.stem: An auditor asks Fabrikam for evidence of which users accepted or declined the Partner Agreement terms of use. What should you review?
choices: The risky users report in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
The provisioning logs for the partner application
The terms of use acceptance details and audit logs
The access review history for guest users
questions.answer: The terms of use acceptance details and audit logs
questions.explanation: Terms of use keeps per-user accept and decline records, and the related audit log entries show when each action happened. ID Protection reports track risk, not consent to a document.

questions.stem: Tailspin Toys has employees in France and Japan who must read the terms of use in their own language. What should you do with the LEAST administrative effort?
choices: Create a separate terms of use and policy per country
Translate the document and host it on a public website
Ask users to change their browser language before sign-in
Add a PDF for each language to the same terms of use
questions.answer: Add a PDF for each language to the same terms of use
questions.explanation: One terms of use can hold language versions, and users see the version that matches their language. Separate terms of use and Conditional Access policies per country would work but take more effort to manage.

questions.topic: Connected organizations and external user lifecycle
questions.stem: Litware's project partners use their own Microsoft Entra tenant. Partner users must be able to request the Joint Project access package, and access package policies must be able to target the partner as a known organization. What should you configure FIRST?
choices: Guest invitations for every partner user in advance
A cross-tenant synchronization configuration
A connected organization for the partner tenant
Catalog reader assignments for the partner users
questions.answer: A connected organization for the partner tenant
questions.explanation: A connected organization represents the partner's directory, so policies for users not in your directory can allow its users to request access and be added as guests on approval. Inviting everyone up front defeats the self-service, lifecycle-managed approach.

questions.topic: Connected organizations and external user lifecycle
questions.stem: External users at Contoso are added as guests through entitlement management. When a guest loses the last access package assignment, the guest must be blocked from signing in and removed from the tenant 30 days later. What should you configure?
choices: Entitlement management settings for external users
An access review of all guest users in the tenant
A Conditional Access policy that blocks all guest users
A 30-day expiration on each access package assignment
questions.answer: Entitlement management settings for external users
questions.explanation: Entitlement management settings can block sign-in and remove external users, after a set number of days, when they no longer have any assignments. A 30-day expiration would end access early instead of cleaning up after the last assignment ends.

questions.topic: Connected organizations and external user lifecycle
questions.stem: A connected organization was created automatically at Adatum after a partner user requested an access package through a policy that allows all external users. The organization's users must now be able to request packages that are scoped to All configured connected organizations. What should you do?
choices: Add the partner domain to the B2B collaboration allow list
Move the access package to a new catalog
Assign the partner's sponsors the Catalog owner role
Change the connected organization's state from Proposed to Configured
questions.answer: Change the connected organization's state from Proposed to Configured
questions.explanation: Automatically created connected organizations are in the Proposed state and are not part of the All configured connected organizations scope until an administrator sets them to Configured. Allow lists control invitations, not this policy scope.

questions.topic: Connected organizations and external user lifecycle
questions.stem: No access package in Northwind Traders' Internal HR catalog may ever be requested by external users, even if someone misconfigures a policy later. What should you configure?
choices: Delete all of the tenant's connected organizations
Set the catalog's Enabled for external users setting to No
Remove the Guest Inviter role from all users
Require two approval stages on every policy
questions.answer: Set the catalog's Enabled for external users setting to No
questions.explanation: When a catalog is not enabled for external users, its access packages cannot have policies that let users outside the directory request access. Deleting connected organizations would not stop a policy that allows any external user.

questions.topic: Connected organizations and external user lifecycle
questions.stem: Requests from Fabrikam's partner users must be approved by the partner's own project lead, who is a user in the partner's tenant. What should you configure?
choices: Make the project lead a catalog owner of the catalog
Add the project lead as an external sponsor and use sponsors as approvers
Add the project lead as a fallback reviewer in a recurring guest access review
Assign the project lead the Guest Inviter role
questions.answer: Add the project lead as an external sponsor and use sponsors as approvers
questions.explanation: A connected organization can list internal and external sponsors, and an access package policy can route approval to those sponsors. Making the partner lead a catalog owner would give management rights far beyond approving requests.

questions.stem: Match each entitlement management role to the task it allows.

pairs.match: Add resources to a catalog and manage its roles
Create and edit access packages in a catalog
Add and remove assignments for existing access packages
View a catalog's access packages without changing them

targets_extra: Approve role activations in Privileged Identity Management
questions.explanation: Entitlement management roles are scoped to catalogs and range from creating catalogs down to read-only access. Approving PIM activations belongs to PIM approvers, not to any entitlement management role.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to give a project team self-service access to a group, an application and a SharePoint Online site through entitlement management.
items: Create a catalog for the project
Add the group, application and SharePoint Online site to the catalog
Create an access package and select resource roles from the catalog
Configure a request policy with approvers and expiration
Share the access package's My Access link with eligible users
questions.explanation: Resources must be in a catalog before an access package in that catalog can use them, and the policy decides who can request and for how long. Users can only request once the package and its policy exist.

questions.stem: Match each access package approval setting to its effect.

pairs.match: Used when the manager or sponsor approver cannot be found
Receive the request when the first approvers do not decide in time
Approvers must give a reason for their decision
Requesters must explain why they need access

targets_extra: Users must accept a terms of use document
questions.explanation: Fallback approvers cover a missing approver, while alternate approvers cover a slow one. Justification settings capture reasons from approvers or requesters; terms of use acceptance is a Conditional Access control.

questions.topic: Connected organizations and external user lifecycle
questions.stem: External users at Wingtip Toys are added through access packages. When an external user's last assignment ends, the account must be cleaned up automatically. Which TWO entitlement management settings should you configure?
choices: Block external user from signing in to this directory
Remove external user
A self-service sign-up user flow for guests
Inbound cross-tenant access settings that require MFA
Mark the catalog's access packages as hidden
answers: Block external user from signing in to this directory
questions.explanation: The external user lifecycle settings block sign-in and then remove the guest after a set number of days once the last assignment is gone. Sign-up user flows and cross-tenant MFA settings govern how users arrive, not how they are cleaned up.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of access reviews in Microsoft Entra ID Governance?
choices: To detect sign-ins that come from anonymous IP addresses
To approve user requests for new access packages
To block legacy authentication protocols for all users
To regularly confirm that users still need their access
questions.answer: To regularly confirm that users still need their access
questions.explanation: Access reviews let reviewers attest to group memberships, application assignments, access package assignments and role assignments so unneeded access can be removed. Detecting risky sign-ins is a Microsoft Entra ID Protection function.

questions.stem: Contoso plans to review the members of several security groups every quarter. Which license is required for the users involved in the reviews?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID P2
Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P1
Microsoft 365 Business Basic
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID P2
questions.explanation: Access reviews require Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance licenses. Microsoft Entra ID P1 covers features such as Conditional Access but not access reviews.

questions.stem: An administrator at Adatum must create access reviews of security groups and enterprise applications. Which role should you assign, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Global Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
Identity Governance Administrator
Security Administrator
questions.answer: Identity Governance Administrator
questions.explanation: Identity Governance Administrator can create and manage access reviews of groups and applications, as well as entitlement management. Global Administrator could also do it but grants far more than needed.

questions.stem: Fabrikam must review who holds the Global Administrator and Exchange Administrator roles every quarter. Role assignments are managed in Privileged Identity Management (PIM). Which role should you assign to the person who creates these reviews, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Global Administrator
User Administrator
Security Reader
Privileged Role Administrator
questions.answer: Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explanation: Reviews of Microsoft Entra roles are created through PIM, which Privileged Role Administrator can manage. User Administrator cannot manage privileged role assignments or their reviews.

questions.stem: Group owners at Tailspin Toys want to create and manage access reviews for the groups they own, without being given any administrator role. What should you do?
choices: Assign each owner the Identity Governance Administrator role
Make each group owner a catalog owner in entitlement management for their groups
Turn on the access review setting that lets group owners create reviews
Assign each owner the Groups Administrator role
questions.answer: Turn on the access review setting that lets group owners create reviews
questions.explanation: An access reviews setting lets group owners create and manage reviews for the groups they own. Assigning an administrator role to each owner breaks the requirement and grants tenant-wide rights.

questions.stem: Northwind Traders wants to review which users are eligible for or assigned to the Billing Reader role on an Azure subscription. Where should this review be created?
choices: As a Teams + Groups review of the group that holds the subscription owners
In Privileged Identity Management for Azure resource roles
As an access package review in entitlement management
As an Applications review of the Azure portal app
questions.answer: In Privileged Identity Management for Azure resource roles
questions.explanation: Reviews of Azure resource role assignments are created through PIM for Azure resources. A Teams + Groups review covers group membership, not Azure role assignments made directly to users.

questions.stem: Litware wants owners of every Microsoft 365 group that contains guests to review only the guests in their group. Which review scope should you configure?
choices: Teams + Groups, all Microsoft 365 groups with guests, guest users only
Teams + Groups, selected teams and groups, all users
Applications, all enterprise applications that have guests, guest users only
Access packages, all access packages, all users
questions.answer: Teams + Groups, all Microsoft 365 groups with guests, guest users only
questions.explanation: The all Microsoft 365 groups with guest users option creates a review for each such group, and limiting the users to guests leaves members out. Selecting all users would make owners review employees as well.

questions.stem: Contoso must review which users are assigned to its Salesforce enterprise application, which uses user assignment. What should you select as what to review?
choices: Applications, then the Salesforce enterprise application
Teams + Groups, then a group named Salesforce Users
Access packages, then the default catalog
Microsoft Entra roles, then the Application Administrator role holders
questions.answer: Applications, then the Salesforce enterprise application
questions.explanation: An Applications review covers the users and groups assigned to the enterprise application. Reviewing one group would miss users assigned to the application directly.

questions.stem: Adatum wants a review of a large group to include only members who have not signed in for 90 days, so reviewers can focus on stale accounts. What should you configure?
choices: Scope the review to guest users only
Scope the review to inactive users (90 days)
Set the review's duration to 90 days
Set the review's recurrence to quarterly with auto apply turned on
questions.answer: Scope the review to inactive users (90 days)
questions.explanation: The inactive users option limits the reviewees to users with no sign-in during the chosen number of days. Duration and recurrence control timing, not which users are reviewed.

questions.stem: Assignments to Fabrikam's Partner Portal access package must be reviewed, and users who are denied must lose the entire access package. What should you select as what to review?
choices: Teams + Groups, then each group in the package
Applications, then the My Access portal
Access packages, then the Partner Portal access package
Azure resource roles, then the subscription used by the partner portal
questions.answer: Access packages, then the Partner Portal access package
questions.explanation: Reviewing the access package removes the denied users' package assignments, which also removes the resources it granted. Reviewing the groups would only remove group membership while the package assignment stays.

questions.stem: An access review of a group uses the Guest users only scope. Which users are included in the review?
choices: Only users from configured connected organizations
Guests plus members who have never signed in
Only guests who were invited in the last 30 days
Users in the group whose user type is Guest
questions.answer: Users in the group whose user type is Guest
questions.explanation: The guest scope includes the resource's users with the Guest user type, however they were invited. It is not limited to connected organizations or to recent invitations.

questions.stem: Wingtip Toys wants each guest user to confirm whether they still need access to the Projects team. Which reviewer option should you choose?
choices: Managers of users
Group owners
Users review their own access
Selected users or groups
questions.answer: Users review their own access
questions.explanation: A self-review asks each user to attest to their own continued need, which suits guests who have no manager in the tenant. Managers of users would fail for most guests because they have no manager set.

questions.stem: Managers at Contoso must review their direct reports' access to the Expenses application, but some users have no manager set in Microsoft Entra ID. What should you configure?
choices: Managers of users as reviewers, with fallback reviewers
Users review their own access, with fallback reviewers
Group owners as reviewers, without fallback reviewers
The Global Administrator as the only selected reviewer for all users
questions.answer: Managers of users as reviewers, with fallback reviewers
questions.explanation: Fallback reviewers take over the review of users whose manager cannot be found. Without them, users with no manager would not be reviewed by anyone.

questions.stem: At Adatum, managers must review access to the Finance app first, and then the app owner must review only the users that managers approved. What should you configure?
choices: One stage that lists both the managers and the app owner as the reviewers
Two separate reviews that start on the same date
A self-review followed by a manual export to the app owner
A multi-stage review that passes only approved users to the second stage
questions.answer: A multi-stage review that passes only approved users to the second stage
questions.explanation: Multi-stage reviews run stages in sequence, and you can choose which reviewees, such as those approved, go to the next stage. In a single stage with several reviewers, any one reviewer's decision would stand.

questions.stem: Several reviewers are assigned to the same stage of an access review, and two of them give different decisions for one user. Which decision is recorded?
choices: The first decision submitted by any reviewer
The last decision submitted by any reviewer
The decision of the reviewer listed first
Deny, because the reviewers disagreed
questions.answer: The last decision submitted by any reviewer
questions.explanation: When multiple reviewers can review the same user, the most recent decision is recorded. There is no majority or automatic deny when reviewers disagree.

questions.stem: Litware is creating one access review that covers every Microsoft 365 group with guests. Each group must be reviewed by the people who own that group. Which reviewer option requires the LEAST administrative effort?
choices: Selected users or groups
Group owners
Managers of users
Users review their own access
questions.answer: Group owners
questions.explanation: Group owners routes each group's review to that group's owners automatically. Selected users or groups would need one fixed set of reviewers for all groups.

questions.stem: At the end of an access review at Fabrikam, users who were denied must lose access to the group without an administrator taking any further action. What should you enable?
choices: If reviewers don't respond: Remove access
Reminders to reviewers by email
Justification required for every decision
Auto apply results to resource
questions.answer: Auto apply results to resource
questions.explanation: Auto apply removes denied users from the resource when the review completes. The If reviewers don't respond setting only decides what happens to users with no decision; it does not apply the denied ones by itself.

questions.stem: Reviewers at Tailspin Toys often ignore access reviews of guest users. Company policy says a guest with no decision at the end of a review must lose access. Which option should you set for If reviewers don't respond?
choices: Remove access
No change
Approve access
Take recommendations
questions.answer: Remove access
questions.explanation: Remove access denies every unreviewed user, and with auto apply turned on the access is removed. Take recommendations could keep guests who signed in recently, which breaks the policy.

questions.stem: A review of guest users at Northwind Traders must ensure that denied guests can no longer sign in and are later deleted from the tenant. Which action should you configure for denied guest users?
choices: Remove user's membership from the resource
Disable the user's account in the user's home tenant
Block user from signing-in for 30 days, then remove user from the tenant
Delete the group that the denied guests are members of after the review ends
questions.answer: Block user from signing-in for 30 days, then remove user from the tenant
questions.explanation: For reviews scoped to guests, you can block denied guests from signing in and then remove them from the tenant after 30 days. Removing membership only takes them out of the resource; the guest account stays.

questions.stem: Contoso must review a group every three months, and reviewers must have two weeks to finish each review. How should you configure the review?
choices: Monthly recurrence with a duration of 14 days
Quarterly recurrence with a duration of 90 days
Annual recurrence with a duration of 14 days
Quarterly recurrence with a duration of 14 days
questions.answer: Quarterly recurrence with a duration of 14 days
questions.explanation: Recurrence sets how often a new instance starts, and duration sets how long reviewers have to finish it. A 90-day duration would run each review for the whole quarter instead of two weeks.

questions.stem: Reviewers at Adatum want the review to suggest denying users who have not signed in recently. What should you enable in the review settings?
choices: Auto apply results to resource
Justification required
The no sign-in decision helper for reviewers
Additional content for the reviewer notification email
questions.answer: The no sign-in decision helper for reviewers
questions.explanation: Reviewer decision helpers show recommendations, such as deny for users with no recent sign-in. Auto apply only acts on decisions after the review ends; it does not help reviewers decide.

questions.stem: Litware wants users who are not reviewed by the end of an access review to receive the system's suggested decision, based on their recent activity. Which option should you set for If reviewers don't respond?
choices: Remove access
Take recommendations
Approve access
No change
questions.answer: Take recommendations
questions.explanation: Take recommendations applies the recommended decision, such as approve for recently active users and deny for inactive ones, to each unreviewed user. No change leaves everyone's access as it was.

questions.stem: Wingtip Toys' auditors require reviewers to explain every Approve decision in an access review. What should you enable?
choices: Justification required
Mail notifications
Reminders
Auto apply results to resource
questions.answer: Justification required
questions.explanation: With justification required, reviewers must enter a reason when they approve access. Mail notifications and reminders only tell reviewers that a review needs attention.

questions.stem: The compliance team at Fabrikam must be told by email whenever a quarterly access review of the Finance group ends. What should you configure in the review's completion settings?
choices: Send a notification at the end of the review to the compliance team
Add the compliance team as fallback reviewers
Add the compliance team as group owners of the Finance group so they get emails
Turn on reminders for the compliance team
questions.answer: Send a notification at the end of the review to the compliance team
questions.explanation: A review can send a notification to other users or groups when it ends, with a link to the results. Fallback reviewers would ask the compliance team to make decisions, which is not what was requested.

questions.stem: Halfway through an access review, an administrator at Contoso wants to see how many users have been approved, denied or not yet reviewed. What should the administrator use?
choices: The Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
The access review's overview and results pages
The risky users report in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
The Identity Secure Score dashboard
questions.answer: The access review's overview and results pages
questions.explanation: The overview of an active review shows progress, including counts of approved, denied and unreviewed users, and the results page lists each decision. Sign-in logs and risk reports do not track review decisions.

questions.stem: Several reviewers at Adatum have not started an access review that ends in three days. What should the administrator do FIRST?
choices: Stop the review and create a new one with a longer duration
Reset all decisions in the review
Send a reminder to the reviewers from the review
Change the review to a self-review
questions.answer: Send a reminder to the reviewers from the review
questions.explanation: A reminder emails the reviewers who have not finished, without disturbing decisions already made. Stopping or resetting the review would discard progress or end it early.

questions.stem: After a quarterly review of the Payroll group completes, an auditor at Tailspin Toys asks for a file that lists every reviewer decision. What should you do?
choices: Export the sign-in logs for the Payroll group members
Export the group's current membership as a file
Open the audit logs for the Group Management category
Download the results of the completed review instance
questions.answer: Download the results of the completed review instance
questions.explanation: The results of a review instance can be downloaded and show each user, the decision, the reviewer and any justification. Current membership shows who has access now, not what reviewers decided.

questions.stem: Northwind Traders needs one report of all access review decisions made across many reviews over the past year for an annual audit. What should you use?
choices: The Identity Secure Score history
A Conditional Access insights workbook
An access review history report
The provisioning logs for each application
questions.answer: An access review history report
questions.explanation: Review history reports collect the decisions from multiple access reviews over a chosen date range into a downloadable report. Secure Score history measures security posture, not review outcomes.

questions.stem: Litware must keep access review audit events for two years and query them with KQL together with other identity logs. What should you configure?
choices: Diagnostic settings that send audit logs to a Log Analytics workspace
A longer recurrence on each access review
Monthly downloads of each review's results, stored on a secure file share
Email notifications to the security team
questions.answer: Diagnostic settings that send audit logs to a Log Analytics workspace
questions.explanation: Diagnostic settings stream Microsoft Entra audit logs, including access review events, to Log Analytics, where retention is configurable and KQL queries can run. Monthly downloads would not support KQL or central retention.

questions.stem: An administrator at Wingtip Toys wants to find out who stopped an access review of the Sales group early. What should you check?
choices: The sign-in logs filtered by the Sales group
The access review's list of reviewee decisions and reviewer names
The Sales group's membership change history
The Microsoft Entra audit logs for access review activity
questions.answer: The Microsoft Entra audit logs for access review activity
questions.explanation: Changes to access reviews, such as stopping one, are recorded in the audit logs with the actor. The list of decisions shows what reviewers decided, not who changed the review itself.

questions.stem: A manager at Contoso receives an email asking her to complete an access review of her team. Where does she review and record her decisions?
choices: The My Apps portal
The My Access portal
The My Account portal
The Microsoft 365 admin center
questions.answer: The My Access portal
questions.explanation: Reviewers complete their assigned access reviews in My Access, which the review email links to. My Account manages a user's own sign-in and security information.

questions.stem: A reviewer at Fabrikam agrees with every recommendation shown for the 200 users in her review. What should she do with the LEAST effort?
choices: Approve or deny each user one at a time
Accept the recommendations for the reviewed users
Download the users and send them to the administrator
Ask the administrator to stop the review
questions.answer: Accept the recommendations for the reviewed users
questions.explanation: Accepting recommendations applies the suggested decision to all users in one action. Deciding one user at a time gives the same result with much more effort.

questions.stem: An access review of the Contractors group at Adatum has completed. Auto apply was not enabled, and the denied users are still members. What should you do with the LEAST administrative effort?
choices: Remove the denied users from the group one at a time
Reset the review and run it again
Create a new review with auto apply turned on
Apply the results from the completed review
questions.answer: Apply the results from the completed review
questions.explanation: When auto apply is off, an administrator can apply the results of a completed review to remove denied users. Removing them by hand works but takes more effort and leaves no link to the review.

questions.stem: A reviewer at Tailspin Toys denied a user by mistake. The access review is still active. What should the reviewer do?
choices: Change the decision for that user before the review ends
Ask an administrator to stop the review and then create it again
Wait until the review ends and then re-add the user
Ask an administrator to reset every decision
questions.answer: Change the decision for that user before the review ends
questions.explanation: Reviewers can change their decisions while the review is still in progress, and only the final decision is applied. Resetting every decision would throw away the rest of the reviewer's work.

questions.stem: Leadership at Northwind Traders wants an active access review ended today so its results can be applied immediately, instead of waiting for the scheduled end date. What should the administrator do FIRST?
choices: Reset the review
Delete the review
Stop the review
Send a reminder
questions.answer: Stop the review
questions.explanation: Stopping a review ends it early so the decisions made so far can be applied. Deleting it would discard the decisions, and resetting clears them while the review keeps running.

questions.stem: A reviewer at Litware does not know whether a contractor still needs access to the Design group and wants to record that uncertainty instead of guessing. Which decision should the reviewer choose?
choices: Approve
Deny
Skip
Don't know
questions.answer: Don't know
questions.explanation: Don't know records that the reviewer cannot decide, and an optional justification can explain why. Approving or denying would record a decision the reviewer cannot support.

questions.stem: Reviewers at Wingtip Toys made decisions in an active access review based on an outdated list of contractors. The administrator wants to clear all decisions so reviewers can start again, while the review stays active. What should the administrator do?
choices: Stop the review
Apply the results
Reset the decisions in the review
Delete the review
questions.answer: Reset the decisions in the review
questions.explanation: Resetting an active review clears the decisions made so far, and reviewers can review again. Stopping the review would end it with the outdated decisions in place.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to create a recurring access review of guest users in a Microsoft 365 group.
items: Select Teams + Groups and choose the group to review
Limit the review scope to guest users only
Choose the reviewers and any fallback reviewers
Set the start date, recurrence and duration
Configure completion settings such as auto apply
Review the settings and create the access review
questions.explanation: The review wizard starts with what to review and the scope of users, then the reviewers and schedule, then the completion and advanced settings. Creating the review is the last step, after every setting is chosen.

questions.stem: An administrator at Contoso is creating an access review in Microsoft Entra ID Governance. Which TWO can the administrator choose as what to review?
choices: Teams + Groups
Applications
Conditional Access policies
Named locations
Authentication methods policies
questions.explanation: Access reviews cover access to resources, such as group membership and application assignment, as well as access packages and roles. Conditional Access policies, named locations and authentication methods are configuration objects, not access that users hold.

questions.stem: Which TWO reviewer options in an access review can use fallback reviewers when the expected reviewer cannot be found?
choices: Managers of users
Group owners
Users review their own access
Selected users or groups
Catalog readers
questions.explanation: Fallback reviewers step in when a user has no manager or a group has no owner. Self-review and selected reviewers always resolve to a known reviewer, so fallback reviewers do not apply to them.

questions.stem: Match each If reviewers don't respond option to what happens to unreviewed users when the review ends.

pairs.match: Unreviewed users are denied and lose access
Unreviewed users are marked as approved
Each unreviewed user gets the suggested decision

targets_extra: Unreviewed users are converted to member users
questions.explanation: The option decides the outcome for users no reviewer acted on, and it takes effect on the resource when results are applied. No option changes a user's type.
